paras.text: Thus, a mixture of all the four substitution products i.e. methyl chloride, methylene chloride, chloroform and carbon tetrachloride are obtained. The extent of their concentration in the mixture depends on the relative amounts of chlorine and methane. If chlorine is taken in excess, the reaction goes to the final substitution product and carbon tetrachloride is the major product. On the contrary, when chlorine is limited and methane is in excess, the major product of the reaction is methyl chloride.

paras.text: Oxidation generally refers to the increase in oxidation state of an atom. Oxidation of organic compounds corresponds to an increase in the oxidation state of carbon. Oxidation of carbon occurs when a bond between carbon and an atom which is less electronegative than carbon is replaced by a bond to an atom that is more electronegative than carbon (in substitution reactions). Oxidation state of carbon increases with increase in the number of bonds between carbon and oxygen and decreases the number of carbon-hydrogen bonds, as shown in Table 16.4. We can extend the generalization that any element more electronegative than carbon will have the same effect on oxidation number as oxygen. Thus, the oxidation numbers of carbon in CH₃Cl and in CH₃OH are the same (−2).

16.4 Oxidation of Organic Compounds

Oxidation generally refers to the increase in oxidation state of an atom. Oxidation of organic compounds corresponds to an increase in the oxidation state of carbon. Oxidation of carbon occurs when a bond between carbon and an atom which is less electronegative than carbon is replaced by a bond to an atom that is more electronegative than carbon (in substitution reactions). Oxidation state of carbon increases with increase in the number of bonds between carbon and oxygen and decreases the number of carbon-hydrogen bonds, as shown in Table 16.4. We can extend the generalization that any element more electronegative than carbon will have the same effect on oxidation number as oxygen. Thus, the oxidation numbers of carbon in CH₃Cl and in CH₃OH are the same (−2).

Table 16.4 Oxidation Number of Carbon in One-Carbon Compounds

Combustion of alkanes is an important reaction, which is also a type of oxidation reaction. Alkanes (and also other hydrocarbons), burn in air to produce carbon dioxide and water. The reaction is highly exothermic and large quantity of heat is evolved. The heat released on complete combustion of a substance is called its heat of combustion. For example,

CH₄ + 2O₂ ⟶ CO₂ + 2H₂O + 890.95 kJ/mol (ignition)

The reaction is of high significance, as it provides basis for their use as fuels to get heat and power. When there is an insufficient supply of oxygen, alkanes on combustion, form carbon monoxide and water or carbon soot and water.

2CH₄ + 3O₂ (limited) ⟶ 2CO + 4H₂O + heat (ignition)

CH₄ + O₂ (very limited) ⟶ C + 2H₂O + heat (ignition)

Methane on heating at high pressure, with a regulated supply of oxygen and in the presence of a suitable catalyst, provides a variety of products like methyl alcohol etc. For example, when a mixture of methane and air is passed over copper catalyst at a temperature 250°C and pressure of 100 atm, as a result, by controlled oxidation process, methane is converted to methanol. Later on this methyl alcohol by controlled oxidation, can be further converted to formaldehyde.

2CH₄ + O₂ ⟶ 2CH₃OH (Cu/250°C/100 atm)

16.5 Alkenes

Alkenes are the unsaturated hydrocarbons which contain a carbon-carbon double bond. They can be represented by the general formula CₙH₂ₙ. They are also known as olefins; derived from Latin oleum meaning ‘oil’ and ficare meaning ‘to form’, because their lower members form oily derivatives on treatment with chlorine or bromine.

16.5.1 Nomenclature

There are two systems for naming alkenes i.e. Common and IUPAC system.

(a) Common System

The common names of fist four members are derived from those of the corresponding alkanes by replacing the ending “ane” with “–ylene”.

2CH₄ + 3O₂ (محدود) ⟶ 2CO + 4H₂O + حرارت (آگ لگانا)

CH₄ + O₂ (بہت محدود) ⟶ C + 2H₂O + حرارت (آگ لگانا)

میتھین کو زیادہ دباؤ پر، آکسیجن کی منضبط فراہمی کے ساتھ اور مناسب عمل انگیز کی موجودگی میں گرم کرنے سے میتھائل الکوحل وغیرہ جیسی مختلف مصنوعات حاصل ہوتی ہیں۔ مثلاً جب میتھین اور ہوا کے آمیزے کو 250°C درجہ حرارت اور 100 atm دباؤ پر تانبے کے عمل انگیز کے اوپر سے گزارا جائے تو منضبط تکسید کے عمل کے نتیجے میں میتھین میتھانول میں تبدیل ہو جاتی ہے۔ بعد میں اس میتھائل الکوحل کو منضبط تکسید سے مزید فارملڈیہائیڈ میں تبدیل کیا جا سکتا ہے۔

2CH₄ + O₂ ⟶ 2CH₃OH (Cu/250°C/100 atm)

16.5 الکینز (دوہرے بند والے)

الکینز غیر سیر شدہ ہائیڈروکاربن ہیں جن میں کاربن–کاربن دوہرا بند ہوتا ہے۔ انہیں عمومی فارمولے CₙH₂ₙ سے ظاہر کیا جا سکتا ہے۔ انہیں اولیفنز بھی کہتے ہیں؛ یہ نام لاطینی الفاظ oleum، یعنی ”تیل“ اور ficare، یعنی ”بنانا“ سے اخذ کیا گیا ہے، کیونکہ ان کے ابتدائی ارکان کلورین یا برومین کے ساتھ عمل کرنے پر تیل جیسے مشتقات بناتے ہیں۔

د الکانونو سوځېدل یو مهم تعامل دی چې د اکسیدېشن د تعامل یو ډول هم دی. الکانونه (او نور هایدروکاربنونه هم) په هوا کې سوځي او کاربن ډای اکسایډ او اوبه جوړوي. دا تعامل ډېر تودوخه خارجوونکی دی او ډېره تودوخه خوشې کېږي. د یوه مادې د بشپړ سوځېدو پر مهال خوشې شوې تودوخه د هغې د سوځېدو تودوخه بلل کېږي. د بېلګې په توګه،

CH₄ + 2O₂ ⟶ CO₂ + 2H₂O + 890.95 kJ/mol (بلول)

دا تعامل ډېر اهمیت لري، ځکه د تودوخې او ځواک د ترلاسه کولو لپاره د سون په توګه د هغوی د کارولو بنسټ برابروي. کله چې د اکسیجن رسونه ناکافي وي، الکانونه د سوځېدو پر مهال کاربن مونو اکسایډ او اوبه یا د کاربن دوده او اوبه جوړوي.

2CH₄ + 3O₂ (محدود) ⟶ 2CO + 4H₂O + تودوخه (بلول)

CH₄ + O₂ (ډېر محدود) ⟶ C + 2H₂O + تودوخه (بلول)

میتان په لوړ فشار کې، د اکسیجن له کنټرول شوې رسونې سره او د مناسب کتلېست په شتون کې د تودولو پر مهال د میتیل الکول او نورو په څېر بېلابېل محصولات ورکوي. د بېلګې په توګه، کله چې د میتان او هوا مخلوط په 250°C تودوخه او 100 atm فشار کې د مسو پر کتلېست تېر شي، د کنټرول شوي اکسیدېشن د پروسې په پایله کې میتان په میتانول بدلېږي. وروسته دا میتیل الکول د کنټرول شوي اکسیدېشن له لارې لا په فارملډیهایډ بدلېدای شي.

2CH₄ + O₂ ⟶ 2CH₃OH (Cu/250°C/100 atm)

16.5 الکینونه

الکینونه نامشبوع هایدروکاربنونه دي چې د کاربن–کاربن دوه ګونی تړون لري. هغوی په عمومي فورمول CₙH₂ₙ ښودل کېدای شي. هغوی د اولیفینونو په نوم هم پېژندل کېږي؛ دا نوم له لاتیني oleum څخه چې «تېل» معنا لري او ficare څخه چې «جوړول» معنا لري اخیستل شوی، ځکه د هغوی ټیټ غړي له کلورین یا برومین سره د تعامل پر مهال غوړ مشتقات جوړوي.

16.5.1 نومول

د الکینونو د نومولو دوه سیستمونه شته، یعنې عام سیستم او د IUPAC سیستم.

(a) عام سیستم

د لومړیو څلورو غړو عام نومونه د اړوندو الکانونو له نومونو څخه د پای «ane» په «–ylene» بدلولو سره اخیستل کېږي.

CH₂Cl₂ + Cl₂ ⟶ CHCl₃ + HCl

chloroform (trichloromethane)

CHCl₃ + Cl₂ ⟶ CCl₄ + HCl

carbon tetrachloride (tetrachloromethane)

Thus, a mixture of all the four substitution products i.e. methyl chloride, methylene chloride, chloroform and carbon tetrachloride are obtained. The extent of their concentration in the mixture depends on the relative amounts of chlorine and methane. If chlorine is taken in excess, the reaction goes to the final substitution product and carbon tetrachloride is the major product. On the contrary, when chlorine is limited and methane is in excess, the major product of the reaction is methyl chloride.

Tidbit

Mechanism is the step-wise description of a chemical reaction.

16.4 Oxidation of Organic Compounds

Oxidation generally refers to the increase in oxidation state of an atom. Oxidation of organic compounds corresponds to an increase in the oxidation state of carbon. Oxidation of carbon occurs when a bond between carbon and an atom which is less electronegative than carbon is replaced by a bond to an atom that is more electronegative than carbon (in substitution reactions). Oxidation state of carbon increases with increase in the number of bonds between carbon and oxygen and decreases the number of carbon-hydrogen bonds, as shown in Table 16.4. We can extend the generalization that any element more electronegative than carbon will have the same effect on oxidation number as oxygen. Thus, the oxidation numbers of carbon in CH₃Cl and in CH₃OH are the same (−2).

Table 16.4 Oxidation Number of Carbon in One-Carbon Compounds

Combustion of alkanes is an important reaction, which is also a type of oxidation reaction. Alkanes (and also other hydrocarbons), burn in air to produce carbon dioxide and water. The reaction is highly exothermic and large quantity of heat is evolved. The heat released on complete combustion of a substance is called its heat of combustion. For example,

CH₄ + 2O₂ ⟶ CO₂ + 2H₂O + 890.95 kJ/mol (ignition)

The reaction is of high significance, as it provides basis for their use as fuels to get heat and power. When there is an insufficient supply of oxygen, alkanes on combustion, form carbon monoxide and water or carbon soot and water.

2CH₄ + 3O₂ (limited) ⟶ 2CO + 4H₂O + heat (ignition)

CH₄ + O₂ (very limited) ⟶ C + 2H₂O + heat (ignition)

Methane on heating at high pressure, with a regulated supply of oxygen and in the presence of a suitable catalyst, provides a variety of products like methyl alcohol etc. For example, when a mixture of methane and air is passed over copper catalyst at a temperature 250°C and pressure of 100 atm, as a result, by controlled oxidation process, methane is converted to methanol. Later on this methyl alcohol by controlled oxidation, can be further converted to formaldehyde.

2CH₄ + O₂ ⟶ 2CH₃OH (Cu/250°C/100 atm)

16.5 Alkenes

Alkenes are the unsaturated hydrocarbons which contain a carbon-carbon double bond. They can be represented by the general formula CₙH₂ₙ. They are also known as olefins; derived from Latin oleum meaning ‘oil’ and ficare meaning ‘to form’, because their lower members form oily derivatives on treatment with chlorine or bromine.

16.5.1 Nomenclature

There are two systems for naming alkenes i.e. Common and IUPAC system.

(a) Common System

The common names of fist four members are derived from those of the corresponding alkanes by replacing the ending “ane” with “–ylene”.
